tb21_profile.skill: Read text out of scanned JPGs and PDFs (OCR plus PDF text extraction), classify each document by its content, pull labelled monetary fields out of noisy layouts under disambiguation rules, and aggregate into an exact-schema CSV
tb21_profile.domain: Document/OCR processing in Python (tesseract, pdftotext/pdfplumber), invoice and VAT/tax data extraction, CSV reporting
tb21_profile.task_form: build a multi-stage batch pipeline over a directory: classify -> move files -> extract fields -> emit a CSV with a computed totals row, leaving the source directory empty

searches: tools.py search all (?i)\binvoice|\breceipt|\bVAT\b|sales tax|grand total|amount due
tools.py search rts (?i)summary\.csv|write.{0,20}CSV|CSV file with columns
tools.py words tmax OCR tesseract image extract total amount CSV summary classify documents

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: extract_tables is broken in the cell-construction step; repairing it means understanding how table structure is recovered from a PDF page.
extract_text(layout=True) fails; layout-preserving text extraction is how labelled amounts stay associated with their labels on an invoice.
Tolerance-based clustering groups characters into lines and columns; getting it wrong is exactly why a 'Total' value lands on the wrong row.
obj_to_edges breaks explicit table strategies; edge detection is the machinery behind pulling rows out of an invoice table.
extract_words mishandles rotated text; orientation handling is a real failure mode when reading scanned or rotated documents.
CCITT G4 decoder emits wrong bit patterns - that codec is exactly what scanned-image PDFs use, so it gates reading scans at all.
Table object loses its rows/columns accessors; API-level repair inside the PDF table-extraction library used for this kind of task.
LZW decoder failure blocks text and image extraction from compressed PDFs; the stream layer under every PDF text read.
pdfplumber's CLI mishandles page ranges and formatting flags; same library driven as a batch command-line extractor.
Opening a PDF by path versus file object is inverted; small, but it is the entry point of every batch PDF walk.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Import ragged CSV of the exact kind Tabula emits when extracting tables from PDFs; handling missing trailing cells in extracted invoice tables.
Regression in the PyPDF2 writer's stream handling; same Python PDF stack this task's PDF branch runs on.
A CSV ingest must accept column headings in any case; label normalization is what makes 'Total' vs 'TOTAL' vs 'Grand Total' resolvable.
PDF XMP metadata date parsing is wrong; extracting a typed value out of a PDF's own metadata strings.
The wrong column is passed into the row-key builder of a csv-to-model converter; a field-mapping bug of the kind that silently corrupts a summary.
read_csv breaks when combining iterator and nrows; the CSV reader at the core of any tabular summary step.
usecols selects the wrong columns under the pyarrow engine; column selection correctness when assembling a report.
Tabular import from a spreadsheet misbehaves; same dataset-import library family, different input format.
Text comes out duplicated when the PDF is read back; a concrete example of extracted PDF text not matching the document.
Add a CSV export path alongside the existing HTML one; emitting a well-formed CSV report, nothing document-related.

notes: TMax has ~750 OCR tasks but almost all use OCR to read one config value out of a screenshot; I filtered hard for the few that OCR a business document and then build a structured aggregate (task_003095, task_001480, task_002266, task_000226). SWE-Smith is unexpectedly strong because it contains the whole jsvine/pdfplumber repo plus pdfminer.six, which is literally the PDF text/table extraction layer this task needs - none of that was in the shortlist and it all came from my own searches. TerminalWorld has no OCR at all and only one content-classification task (tw_288787); the rest of its ten are CSV-aggregation fillers. RTS has no OCR either; its 'receipt' hits are a large shopping-cart-CLI family that shares the word but not the work, and I kept only two of them, low-scored. SWE-Rebench is the weakest: PyPDF2 and tablib give domain credit but nothing in it does document classification or field extraction.
